headline: ISEZ Closes 2026 Harvest at 486,300 Tonnes of Grain as Silos Fill
dek: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources calls it the best grain total in several seasons, though growers say storage and haulage are now the pinch.
ticker: Grain harvest closes at 486,300 tonnes; Kara-Bulak and Nurzhan stores full
paragraphs: The 2026 grain harvest in the Irad Special Economic Zone is complete and totals 486,300 tonnes, the Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources announced on Saturday. The ministry described it as the best result in several seasons.

Wheat made up the largest share at about 214,000 tonnes, followed by maize at 148,000 tonnes, much of it from the Kara-Bulak and Chu fields. Barley added 71,000 tonnes and Chu rice 31,000 tonnes, with a further 22,300 tonnes of other grains and pulses. The grain came mainly from Chu District, Talas District and the lower plain of Kara-Buura District.

Minister Melis Nurmatov (see *Who's Who in Irad*), who has led the ministry since 2014 and was born in the Chu oasis, credited good spring water and the canal rotations published each April. "Farmers could plan their sowing and their watering because they knew the schedule," he said. "The irrigation modernisation of recent years is now visible in the field, and the farmers of Chu, Talas and Kara-Buura have earned the thanks of the whole Zone."

The size of the crop has brought a pleasant difficulty. The Kara-Bulak depot and the Nurzhan terminal both reported full silos at the end of the harvest, and the surplus that has kept potatoes at 2.10 som a kilo and Chu apples at 3.45 now extends to the grain stores.

Growers say space and lorries, not yields, are the limit. "The wheat came off dry and the crop was good," said Toktosun Abdraev, a Chu oasis farmer near Nurzhan. "Now we wait for haulage and for room in the store. Nobody here is complaining about a big harvest, but we would like it moved."

Dr Myktybek Abylov, an agronomist at Talas State University, welcomed the total but urged caution on what it means for incomes. "A large crop at low som prices does not automatically leave a farmer better off," he said, noting that diesel, at 6.10 som a litre at NurGaz stations, and imported inputs are priced off the dollar.
The ministry said grain will be drawn down through the winter as mills and feed producers take deliveries, with attention now turning to preparing canals and fields for the 2027 sowing.
